method:
Strategy lab: which exits, and which combination of ALL indicators, actually work out of sample?

Long only (the live terminal is long only). Two questions, answered walk-forward so nothing is judged on
the data that chose it:

1. Exits per setup. Every long setup episode is simulated with 7 stops x 10 exits x 5 time stops
   (fixed ATR / R targets and 2 / 2.5 / 3-ATR trailing stops; 5-20 sessions). Each setup's exit is
   chosen on the first 60% of dates (in sample) and judged on the last 40% (out of sample), next to
   random entries with the same exit (so the setup's own edge is visible).

2. Indicator weights. Every setup episode AND a random-entry sample (every 10th session of every stock)
   gets one feature vector of ~170 indicators (src/scanner/model_features.py: moving averages,
   oscillators, volume, relative strength, the 49 analyst techniques, the volume profile / chip
   distribution, market regime). The label is the trade's R with the chosen exit. For each test year,
   models are fitted only on data that ended a month before that year starts:
     ic      sign-consistent information-coefficient weights (a feature counts only if its rank
             correlation with the outcome had the same sign in >= 75% of training years)
     ridge   ridge regression on standardised, winsorised features (penalty chosen on the last 20% of
             the training window)
   Out-of-sample checks: rank correlation of the score with the outcome, average R of the top fifth vs
   all trades, positive years, and whether the top fifth of RANDOM entries does as well (then the setup
   adds nothing beyond the model). A model is adopted only if the top fifth beats the average by
   >= 0.05R with t >= 2 and in most test years.

Options positioning cannot be tested: there is no free history of option chains (the terminal now keeps
its own daily IV record for a later study). Survivorship bias: only today's universe is tested.

verdict: Best common long exit: 1.5 ATR stop + 3-ATR trailing stop, max 20 sessions - in sample +0.19R, out of sample +0.29R (12605 trades); random entries with the same exit +0.25R.
Crash rebound (buy the plunge): 1.5 ATR stop + 3-ATR trailing stop, max 20 sessions - out of sample +0.45R over 702 trades, edge over random entries +0.20R.
Breakout (20D high, volume): 1.0 ATR stop + 3-ATR trailing stop, max 20 sessions - out of sample +0.29R over 1769 trades, edge over random entries +0.01R.
Pullback to EMA9/21 in uptrend: 1.5 ATR stop + 3-ATR trailing stop, max 20 sessions (common exit) - out of sample +0.29R over 4576 trades, edge over random entries +0.04R.
Volatility squeeze near highs: 2.0 ATR stop + 3R target, max 20 sessions - out of sample +0.44R over 304 trades, edge over random entries +0.14R.
EMA21 reclaim: 1.5 ATR stop + 3-ATR trailing stop, max 20 sessions - out of sample +0.25R over 1048 trades, edge over random entries -0.00R.
Momentum leader near highs: 1.5 ATR stop + 3-ATR trailing stop, max 20 sessions (common exit) - out of sample +0.30R over 4178 trades, edge over random entries +0.05R.
139 of 178 indicators kept the same direction of effect out of sample (|rank correlation| >= 0.02); the strongest single indicator correlations are around 0.15.
Ridge model on all indicators: out of sample the top fifth averaged +0.26R vs +0.28R for all setup trades (t -0.2, rank correlation +0.072, better in 33% of test years) - not adopted.
Same model on random entries: top fifth +0.28R vs +0.25R.
Sign-consistent indicator weights: out of sample the top fifth averaged +0.32R vs +0.28R for all setup trades (t 0.7, rank correlation +0.134, better in 33% of test years) - not adopted.
Same model on random entries: top fifth +0.25R vs +0.25R.

Momentum leader near highs only in Bullish / Strong Bullish markets: edge over random entries in the kept regimes -0.04R in sample, +0.06R out of sample; in the dropped regimes -0.32R / +0.02R (those trades still averaged +0.02R / +0.33R) - not adopted (the filter must help in both halves).

Pullback to EMA9/21 in uptrend only in Bullish / Strong Bullish markets: edge over random entries in the kept regimes -0.05R in sample, +0.09R out of sample; in the dropped regimes -0.19R / -0.13R (those trades still averaged +0.16R / +0.19R) - not adopted (the filter must help in both halves).
No indicator combination ranked trades reliably out of sample, so the live ranking keeps the backtest-based setup weighting and the composite score is shown for context only.
survivorship_note: Only stocks in today's universe are tested (survivorship bias).
